conviction_note: Mostly balanced. The peers' cloud prints (Azure +48%, Google Cloud +103%) and Anthropic's ~$65B run-rate point to AWS demand, and AMZN has already given up 3.7% intraday on Alphabet's capex/FCF punishment, the same setup as July before a +15.3% print. Against that, the market is visibly selling 2027-spend signals, and Amazon's call will carry one. The AWS bar is disputed (35% vs 38%), so p_up is only 54 on an 8% abs move, giving +0.64. That sits below the +1.1 findings sum because the capex-guide risk and the AWS-bar dispute weigh more on the sign than on any single finding.
bar: Total revenue: company guide $197.0-202.0B (Q2 release, 2026-07-30), consensus $202.2B. Two sources agree on the consensus: 24/7 Wall St (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/amazon-slides-3-as-alphabets-12-plunge-raises-stakes-for-aws-report-meta-rises-3-microsoft-pulls-back/, $202.25B, EPS $1.97) and Pepperstone (https://pepperstone.com/en/insights/market-analysis/equities/amazon-q3-2026-earnings-preview, ~$202B, EPS $1.96). Operating income: guide $22.5-26.5B. No sourced consensus; HSBC models $27B. AWS, the line the stock trades on, has a DISPUTED bar: 24/7 Wall St 2026-10-29 says $45.68B / +38%, while Pepperstone 2026-10-23 says ~35%. Q2 was +37% ($42.2B). So AWS-dependent findings are capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the $202.2B revenue consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest 0.9% of float, 2.4 days to cover (FINRA settlement 2026-09-30, via https://tapeboard.com/stock/AMZN/short-squeeze). Not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. The baseline seal failed (status 'bars_failed: HTTPError'), so there is no sealed implied move or skew. Saxo (2026-10-27, https://www.home.saxo/content/articles/options/amazon-earnings-between-a-typical-report-and-julys-15-jump-27102026) priced the 250-strike Oct-30 straddle at $19.08, ~7.7% of the $249.09 close: put $9.90, call $9.18. With the put $0.91 in the money, that is roughly parity-neutral, so there is no visible put skew. Pepperstone cites ±7.4%. Price path (Yahoo chart): 254.60 on 10-28 to 245.07 at 14:15 ET 10-29 (−3.7% intraday on Alphabet's −12%). Run-up from the 2026-09-30 close of 249.15 is about −1.6%; from the 10-21 high of 262.37 it is −6.6%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was 'Bullish' with 'Extremely High' message volume on 2026-10-12.

findings.finding: Peer cloud prints since Amazon last spoke both beat on AI-cloud demand. Microsoft (10-28): Azure +48% to $33.17B against a ~45% guide and $32.32B consensus; next-quarter guide 49-50% cc against Street 45.1%; CFO: 'demand exceeds supply'. The same release cites third-party supply delays and capex below consensus at $45.2B. Alphabet (10-28): Google Cloud +103% to $30.7B, operating income $11.1B. The AMZN bar is AWS +35-38% on Q2's +37%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AWS acceleration has driven the big up-moves: Q2 2026 AWS +37% (fastest in 18 quarters) took the stock +15.3%; Q3 2025 AWS reacceleration +9.6% (Saxo series). Beats without AWS acceleration were sold: −8.3% Q2 2025, −5.6% Q4 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were carrying the peer demand read into AMZN, the stock would have held or risen with MSFT's +4% after-hours. Instead it is −3.7% today and MSFT has given back to −2%. The market is pricing peers' capex and FCF, not their cloud growth rates. One counterweight is MSFT's third-party supply delays, which could equally cap AWS; that is netted into this size.
findings.independence: Alphabet's own 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm, 2026-10-28) gives Cloud +103%. Two different companies, but both are proxies for AWS, not AWS's own number.

findings.finding: Anthropic, AWS's anchor AI customer with a >$100B 10-year AWS commitment and ~1GW of Trainium capacity due by end-2026, reached an annualized revenue run-rate above $65B by end-July 2026, more than 7x its end-2025 pace (Bloomberg, 2026-08-18). That is direct-counterparty demand inside AWS's Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same AWS line as above: +15.3% when AWS printed +37% in Q2 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-rate is public and is probably part of why the AWS bar moved from ~35% (Pepperstone 10-23) to ~38% (24/7 Wall St 10-29). That rising bar is the sign the market has partly priced it. What remains is whether AWS capacity let Amazon bill it. Jassy said in July that capacity will not meet all 2026 demand.
findings.independence: Anthropic's own compute announcement (https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-amazon-compute, 2026-04-20) gives the 5GW / ~1GW-by-end-2026 Trainium schedule. Google Cloud's TPU-driven +103% shares the Anthropic-demand driver, so this partly overlaps the peer finding; it is sized small for that reason.

findings.finding: AMZN de-rated into the print on peer read-through: −3.7% intraday on 10-29 (254.60 to 245.07) as Alphabet fell ~12% on an EPS miss ($8.7B equity-securities loss), negative FCF and a signalled 2027 spend increase. That follows −4.6% on 10-22 in a sector AI sell-off. In July the same pattern (AMZN sold on Alphabet's capex shock) preceded a +15.3% print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: stock sold off on Alphabet's July capex read-through, then +15.3% on its own print. One precedent only; over 8 prints it is 4 up, 4 down, typical |move| ~6% (Saxo).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a price fact, so it is the market's own statement. The question is whether the de-rating is about Amazon or about Alphabet's search miss and equity loss, which Amazon does not share. Amazon's consensus EPS excludes Anthropic marks (Pepperstone), so an Alphabet-style 'EPS miss on investment marks' cannot hit the Street number the same way. If the market had already discounted that difference, AMZN would not have fallen a third of Alphabet's move on a day MSFT and META held up.
findings.independence: 24/7 Wall St 2026-10-29 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/amazon-slides-3-as-alphabets-12-plunge-raises-stakes-for-aws-report-meta-rises-3-microsoft-pulls-back/) attributes the AMZN drop to Alphabet; TickerSpark attributes 10-22 to a sector sell-off (https://tickerspark.ai/market/amazon-com-inc-amzn-drops-5-as-ai-stocks-sell-off-1792695973080).

findings.finding: Capex and 2027 spending signal risk. Amazon raised 2026 cash capex to ~$220B in July. Trailing FCF is −$7.6B, long-term debt is $128.9B (from $65.6B at year-end), and management gave no FCF-recovery date. On 10-28/29 the market punished Alphabet for negative FCF and a signalled 'significant' 2027 increase. Amazon's call will very likely carry a 2027 capex direction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 print (Feb 2026), when the ~$200B 2026 capex guide shocked: −5.6% next day (Saxo), −9.7% over two days (Trefis). Q2 2026 capex raise to $220B came with an AWS beat and the stock rose +15.3%. So the capex line is sold when AWS does not accelerate with it.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the −3.7% today is this fear. Not fully priced, because no 2027 number exists yet. If the market had fully discounted a large 2027 step-up, AMZN would trade like GOOGL (−12), not −3.7. Financing question (lesson 4): the money buys capacity against a $496B AWS backlog and a 'not enough capacity for 2026' statement, which is why this is not sized larger. META raised capex the same week and rose 3%.
findings.independence: Pepperstone 2026-10-23 (https://pepperstone.com/en/insights/market-analysis/equities/amazon-q3-2026-earnings-preview) gives the FCF, debt and capex figures. It shares the Alphabet read-through with the positioning finding, but the facts differ: price there, spending signal here.

findings.finding: Q2's operating income carried ~$1.15B that will not repeat: ~$551M of AWS energy-contract gains (in the 39.4% AWS margin) and ~$600M of IEEPA tariff refunds (CFO: 'the bulk' of what Amazon expects). The comparison for Q3's operating margin and AWS margin is flattered by that much.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved instance on this name; one-offs in the AWS margin have not been a line AMZN traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: The company guided Q3 operating income ($22.5-26.5B) knowing these would not repeat, so this sits inside the guide. The only unpriced part is how much sell-side margin models extrapolated the 39.4% AWS margin; UBS's 46% 2027 AWS margin against a 39% consensus (24/7 Wall St) suggests most did not.
findings.independence: Supply Chain Dive on the ~$600M refund and 'bulk received' (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/amazon-to-issue-tariff-refunds-in-limited-set-of-circumstances/826815/).

findings.finding: HSBC (note 2026-10-12) models Q3 revenue $203.3B and operating income $27B, both above the top of guidance ($202B / $26.5B). It cites Amazon beating the top of its operating-profit guide for 15 consecutive quarters; separately, Amazon has beaten EPS in 11 of its last 12 reports (24/7 Wall St).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats are not paid on their own: 3 of the last 11 EPS beats saw the stock fall the next day (24/7 Wall St), and over 8 prints it is 4 up, 4 down.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus already sits at the top of the guide ($202.2B), so the revenue part is priced. The operating-income beat pattern is less visible because no consensus OI number circulates in the previews, though a top-of-range OI print is the market's habit-based expectation. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: 24/7 Wall St 2026-10-29 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/29/alphabet-failed-wall-streets-new-ai-test-amazon-takes-it-tonight/) gives the 11-of-12 beat record.

findings.finding: US card-panel proxy for retail: the Kalshi market on Carbon Arc's September 2026 Amazon card-spend index priced ~16-20% YoY growth (above-116 at ~98%, above-120 at ~8%) as of 2026-10-05. September is a clean month, since Prime Day moved into Q2, set against a total Q3 revenue guide of +9-12% depressed by the Prime Day shift and ~80bp FX.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Retail has not been the swing line recently; AWS is (Saxo, Pepperstone).
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy: a prediction-market price on a third-party panel, not a settled reading or a company number, auto-generated page with internal inconsistencies. If the market believed strong September retail, revenue consensus would sit clearly above $202.2B rather than at the guide's top end.

findings.finding: Amazon cut fewer than 1,000 more corporate roles on 2026-10-07, mostly in Stores (customer service, seller support, retail engineering), extending ~30,000 cuts since October 2025. That is a small cost item for Q4 opex.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measurable reaction attributable to the cost-cut line.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (page; cuts confirmed 2026-10-07; secondary source, Amazon has not disclosed numbers)
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial at Amazon's scale (<1,000 of ~1.5m employees). Filed for completeness.

findings.finding: Investment marks: Amazon carried Anthropic at $190.4B at 30 June and booked a $53.4B pre-tax gain in Q2. Alphabet booked an $8.7B equity-securities LOSS in Q3 (−$0.55 EPS), unnamed. Amazon's GAAP EPS can swing tens of billions either way on Q3 marks, but consensus EPS excludes Anthropic marks (Pepperstone).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026's $53.4B gain came with +15.3%, but that move was attributed to AWS, not the mark.
findings.why_not_priced: Below operating income, sign unknown (no Anthropic priced round found in Q3), with no path to guidance. Alphabet's loss shows headline-EPS misses on marks can trigger algorithmic selling after hours, which is the only reason it is filed. Sized at zero with a range.
findings.independence: Pepperstone 2026-10-23 (https://pepperstone.com/en/insights/market-analysis/equities/amazon-q3-2026-earnings-preview) on the $190.4B carrying value and consensus excluding marks.

baseline_tension: There is no sealed baseline (bars failed). Against the reconstructed one, findings lean mildly long against a neutral straddle and a −3.7% pre-print slide, so they cut against the immediate run-down. The capex-guide risk is the same fear driving that slide, which is why p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): the AWS bar is disputed (35% vs 38%), so the two AWS-dependent findings were capped: peer cloud +0.8 to +0.6, Anthropic +0.6 to +0.4. The revenue bar ($202.2B, two sources plus the guide) stands.
Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): AMZN sold 3 of its last 11 EPS beats and is 4 up / 4 down over 8 prints, so the HSBC above-guide OI finding went +0.4 to +0.3 and p_up went 55 to 54.
Rule 5 (proxy): the card-panel prediction-market finding went +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 7 / proxy-inference: the positioning precedent rests on one July instance, +1.0 to +0.8.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the capex is funding a $496B backlog under stated capacity shortage, and META's capex raise was bought the same week, so the capex-guide negative went −1.5 to −1.2.
Rule 6 (inside guidance): the Q2 one-offs not repeating were already inside the Q3 OI guide, −0.3 to −0.1.
Short interest checked before the negatives (0.9% float, 2.4 DTC): not crowded, no change from that.
